title: Finite coefficient tensor domains and ambient evaluation transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\ge m\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$ with the quotient map [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules over constant coefficient rings on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ on a scheme $T$, and $H_R(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_R(U,V)$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The full subcategory $D^b_{ctf}$ consists of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval $[a,b]$: $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_R^L W)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $W$ and $i\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. The scheme $X$ is Noetherian. If $T\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, it admits a flat constructible complex $P$ supported in $[a,b]$ representing it, and $P\otimes_A B$ is a flat constructible K-flat $B$-complex in the same degrees representing $F_XT$; in particular $F_XT\in D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$ with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. For a morphism $f:Y\to X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, exact etale inverse image preserves bounded constructibility and this Tor interval, and its canonical comparison $f_B^*F_X\cong F_Yf_A^*$ is $B$-linear.

On the ambient derived categories the canonical tensor comparisons $F_X(U\otimes_A^LV)\cong F_XU\otimes_B^LF_XV$, together with the constant-ring unit comparison, make $F_X$ strong symmetric monoidal. They are induced by reassociation on flat-term K-flat models, and agree with successive scalar-extension identifications $(T\otimes_A^LB)\otimes_B^LC\cong T\otimes_A^LC$ for $C=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^r)$, $1\le r\le m$, and with the unit identifications when $n=m$.

There is a natural ambient adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(U,H_A(K,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes_A^LK,M)$, with counit evaluation, and likewise over $B$. Its transpose of reduced evaluation defines a unique map $v_{K,M}:F_XH_A(K,M)\to H_B(F_XK,F_XM)$, using the preceding tensor comparison; this is the arrow of [def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow]. For $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ both endpoints belong to $D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$. No invertibility assertion about this map is included.

proof.text: For $R=A$ or $B$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies geometric module pullback with exact etale inverse image and identifies $f^{-1}R_X$ with $R_Y$. Exactness gives $\mathcal H^i(f_R^*T)=f_R^*\mathcal H^i(T)$ by preservation of kernels and cokernels. These sheaves are constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback] and vanish outside the original cohomological bounds. Pull $P$ of Step 2 back termwise: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] makes each term flat, and [prop-constructible-pullback] makes it constructible; it is still zero outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1) this bounded flat complex is K-flat. For any degree-zero $R_Y$-module sheaf $W$, its ordinary tensor with $W$ therefore computes its derived tensor with $W$, and has zero terms outside $[a,b]$. This proves preservation of the stated Tor interval, as well as bounded constructibility. In Lean use the already proved etale boundedConstructible_leftDerivedUpperStar and torAmplitudeIn_leftDerivedUpperStar APIs, which package this argument. Convert the two bounded-constructibility presentations using their cohomological definitions and the constructible module-sheaf comparison; preserve the exact same Tor endpoints.

proof.text: View $A_X\to B_X$ as a morphism of ringed topoi whose underlying geometric morphism is the identity. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives the natural ambient isomorphism $\mu_{U,V}:F_X(U\otimes_A^LV)\cong F_XU\otimes_B^LF_XV$. More explicitly choose flat-term K-flat models $P,Q$ for arbitrary $U,V$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Their total tensor is again flat-term K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], and their scalar extensions are flat-term K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Consequently every vertex of this comparison is computed by these same models. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit], applied to this ringed-topos morphism, $\mu$ is the unique natural transformation whose component at such $P,Q$ is the localization of the cochain comparison $c_{P,Q}$ of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], composed with the computation and representative isomorphisms. That chain comparison sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, with inverse $(x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes b')\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes bb'$. These are local sheafified tensor generators, not a claim about tensor sheaves being computed on sections.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 0G7E, 07A2 and 07A4; lemma-pullback-tensor-product and its total-complex computation

proof.text: The coefficient-unit comparison is $F_X(A_X[0])\cong B_X[0]$, represented by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$; its inverse sends $b$ to $1\otimes b$. By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], the ambient associators, unitors and symmetry are the signed total-complex constraints. The chain comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] respects exactly these constraints and the scalar-action unit. Thus the associativity, both unit and symmetry diagrams for $\mu$ commute after representing each object by a flat-term K-flat complex as in Step 5. The localized maps in these diagrams are the canonical derived maps by the representative normalization of $\mu$ and of the unit comparison $u$ in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] (which also states both unitor equations). Each derived object has such a representative and the diagrams are natural, so their commutativity on these representatives proves their commutativity on all objects. The same conclusion is stated directly by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the ringed-topos morphism with identity geometric morphism and ring map $A_X\to B_X$: its $t_h,e_h$ make $Lh^*=F_X$ symmetric strong monoidal for the derived associators, both unitors and the signed symmetry. This is the strong symmetric monoidal structure claimed in the statement. Taking inverses gives the tensorator and unit orientation of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor].

source.place: Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived) and Tag 07A4, cochain tensor and scalar-action unit constraints

proof.text: For $A\to B\to C$, [lem-pur-system-scalar-model] supplies the normalized scalar models on this small site, and [lem-pur-system-scalar-coherence] supplies the natural derived composition and identity comparisons with their cochain normalization. On a flat-term K-flat $P$ the first comparison is $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes\bar b c$, and its inverse is $x\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c$. Successive scalar extension is computed on these actual complexes, since [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] applies after each extension. The tensor square is also the composition equation of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] for these identity geometric morphisms. Explicitly both routes send $((x\otimes y)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $(x\otimes\bar b c)\otimes_C(y\otimes1)$, and the unit square multiplies the same scalars. Thus the canonical tensor comparison agrees with successive extension. On the derived level this is the monoidality of the composition comparison $c_{f,g}:P_{gf}\cong P_fP_g$ in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the identity geometric morphisms with ring maps $A_X\to B_X\to C_X$; that comparison is computed by ordinary module pullback composition on flat-term K-flat complexes, hence equals the scalar associator above, normalized on the same models. Its clause on $P_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ gives the case $n=m$. For $n=m$, multiplication $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ gives the identity comparison and the two tensor routes give $(ax)\otimes y=x\otimes(ay)$; the coefficient-unit comparison is multiplication as well. The comparisons are natural derived comparisons by the cited normalization theorem, so these checks prove the assertions on the ambient categories, including nonflat quotient towers.

proof.text: Use the existing finiteHomEtaleClosed record at each coefficient level. Its adjunction is already between the specified right tensor and the published internal Hom. The inverse hom equivalence is tensoring a morphism with the identity followed by the counit evaluation. Applying the hom equivalence to t gives a morphism with that evaluation, and injectivity of the inverse equivalence proves uniqueness. This argument uses arbitrary unbounded objects, with no constructibility or perfection restriction.

Uncurry reduced evaluation with the existing closed record at level m. The equivalence identity (e.symm(v)=t iff v=e(t)) identifies its unique transpose with etaleFiniteHomCanonical, whose body is coefficientBaseChangeHom. For naturality, prove the general closed-calculus identity: uncurry postcomposition by Hom(f,g) using the evaluation_naturality field in f and counit naturality in g. Uncurry precomposition using functoriality of tensor. Uncurry both sides of the coefficient-comparison naturality equation; naturality of the inverse tensor comparison in (Hom(f,g),identity) and (identity,f), followed by naturality of evaluation, makes the results equal. Injectivity of the inverse hom equivalence proves the desired equality. No monoidal coherence or invertibility of the Hom comparison is used. The uncurrying equation is first proved as a small API lemma, after which the comparison definition stays folded. A proved generic conjunction packages these calculations before the single specialization to the finite etale records.
